documents.text: ## Node.js 10, 13, and 15 are no longer supported Node.js 10, 13, 15 all reached end of life either in 2020 or early 2021. ESLint is officially dropping support for these versions of Node.js starting with ESLint v8.0.0. ESLint now supports the following versions of Node.js: - Node.js 12.22 and above - Node.js 14 and above - Node.js 16 and above **To address:** Make sure you upgrade to at least Node.js `12.22.0` when using ESLint v8.0.0. One important thing to double check is the Node.js version supported by your editor when using ESLint via editor integrations. If you are unable to upgrade, we recommend continuing to use ESLint 7 until you are able to upgrade Node.js. **Related issue(s):** [#14023](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/14023)

## Node.js 4 is no longer supported As of April 30th, 2018, Node.js 4 will be at EOL and will no longer be receiving security updates. As a result, we have decided to drop support for it in ESLint v5. We now support the following versions of Node.js: - Node.js 6 (6.14.0 and above) - Node.js 8 (8.10.0 and above) - Anything above Node.js 9.10.0 **To address:** Make sure you upgrade to at least Node.js 6 when using ESLint v5. If you are unable to upgrade, we recommend continuing to use ESLint v4.x until you are able to upgrade Node.js.

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
